title: Where is the multimodal goal post? On the Ability of Foundation Models to Recognize Highlights in Videos
abstract: arXiv:2601.16333v3 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Foundation models are used for many real-world applications involving language understanding and generation from temporally-ordered multimodal events. In this work, we study the ability of models to identify the most important sub-events in a video, which is a fundamental prerequisite for summarizing, reasoning over, or narrating multimodal events. Specifically, we focus on football games and evaluate models on their ability to distinguish between important and non-important sub-events in a game. To this end, we construct a new dataset by leveraging publicly available football highlight reels containing the most important moments of a game according to professional experts, without any additional annotation costs. Using our dataset, we compare several state-of-the-art multimodal models and show that they fail to reliably capture contextual importance. translated_title: 多模态的“球门柱”在哪里？论基础模型识别视频中精彩片段的能力
translated_abstract: 基础模型被广泛应用于许多需要对按时间排序的多模态事件进行语言理解与生成的现实场景中。在这项工作中，我们研究了模型识别视频中最重要的子事件的能力，这是对多模态事件进行总结、推理或叙述的基础前提。具体而言，我们聚焦于足球比赛，评估模型区分比赛中重要与非重要子事件的能力。为此，我们利用公开可得的足球精彩集锦构建了一个新数据集，这些集锦包含了由专业专家认定的比赛最重要时刻，且无需任何额外的标注成本。利用该数据集，我们比较了多个最先进的多模态模型，结果表明它们无法可靠地捕捉上下文重要性。超越标准评估指标的进一步分析揭示了模型的倾向……
tldr: 本研究利用足球比赛官方集锦零成本构建了一个评估数据集，用以测试多模态基础模型识别视频中重要事件的能力，发现现有最先进模型无法可靠地理解事件的上下文重要性。
en_tdlr: This work builds a new zero-annotation-cost dataset from football highlight reels to benchmark multimodal foundation models on identifying important sub-events in videos, showing that state-of-the-art models fail to reliably capture contextual importance.
